gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-lexend-giga: Technical from the first stretched capital, Nulshock draws a steady outline with barely any rise above its lowercase. Lexend Giga follows in plain sans, its flat single-weight lines and generous tracking giving every word room.
gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-lexend-peta:
Nulshock stretches out in a bold, unshaded outline.

Lexend Peta sits beneath in sans-serif, its curves full and its x-height big, so the wide-tracked heading and the tight, sturdy text feel like two sizes of the same confident voice.
gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-lexend-tera: Contemporary in its plotter-pen lines, the body is a quiet foil for Nulshock's bold, stretched outline. Lexend Tera is plain sans with stepping-stone spacing, and that open, widely spaced look is what the two share.
gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-lexend-zetta:
Lexend Zetta is all cut-ribbon strokes and tall small letters.

Nulshock earns its keep big and short, where its stretched, spacious outline and bold technical streak can stand alone without any crowding from the text.
gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-montserrat-altern:
Stretched, widely tracked capitals mark Nulshock out.

Montserrat Alternates answers with sans lowercase that crowds up toward the capital line, and its round letters have rims matching the stems, so the heading's spacious outline gets a snug, compact partner.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-cascadia-code: Origami brings a sign-painter's single-stroke brush look and a lowercase mass like poured lead type. Cascadia Code is its wiry opposite in sans-serif, a monoline skeleton with smooth bends and neighbors standing well apart.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-cascadia-mono:
Cascadia Mono is a plain sans with pin-like letters in a wide board.

Over a longer passage it should feel tidy and compact, capitals blending into lowercase, while Origami's brushy heading supplies the personality the text steps back from.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-julius-sans-one:
Origami has the look of a sign-painter's brush at constant width, with a lowercase heavy as poured lead type.

Julius Sans One is its light, spacious sans foil, all blank space between letters.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-lexend-exa: Origami leads with a sign-painter's single-stroke brush look, its lowercase packed like poured lead type. Lexend Exa then carries a long read in sans, with wide-open curves, a big x-height and stubby ascenders that keep lines steady and distinct.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-lexend-giga: Origami opens with a sign-painter's brush look at constant width, its lowercase packed like poured lead type. And Lexend Giga, in sans-serif, would read as flat, single-weight lines with generous tracking, each word opened up and its ascenders barely clearing the x-height.
